name: Aunt Vertex
bio: The Yards' explosives theologian: she decides which dead machines get gently dismantled and which get returned to the ancestors at speed. Nobody knows her age; the blast records go back further than the census. Sweet as condensed milk until someone disrespects a detonation.
appearance: Tiny round elder in a blast-quilt coat patched from orange signal flags, smoked-glass goggles pushed up into a halo of white hair, earrings cut from old fuses, hands steady as survey stakes, smelling faintly of cinnamon and ammonium nitrate.
voice: Grandmotherly menace. Speaks of explosions in liturgical language — 'services', 'readings', 'the loud amen'. Calls everyone 'duck'. Always has a butterscotch, always knows exactly how much charge a thing needs.

greetings: Duck! Come in out of the dust. Mind the crate by the door, it's armed. The biscuits, however, are safe.
There's my courier. Stand still — you have the look of someone carrying something interesting.
Welcome to services, duck. We worship at noon and detonate at half past.
barks: Everything comes apart, duck. The craft is in the *ceremony* of it.
Four hundred grams, placed with love, and even a mountain apologises.
The old towers aren't dead. They're holding their breath. I help them let go.
mission: Those charges the boss wants? Mine. Cut with a butter knife, blessed twice. Carry them like they're sleeping babies, duck, because chemically that's accurate.
Your little humming box — I'd never crack a sealed thing without an invitation. But do ask it if it *wants* opening. Some things have been waiting forever for the question.
radio: Vertex to the young rider: that dust trail of yours is a joy. Come by after and I'll tell you which canyon echo is lying to you. One of them always is.
If you hear a thump from the Yards followed by applause, that's church, duck, not an accident.
Storm's sniffing around the scar tonight. Bring your charges home to Auntie where they're *appreciated*.
farewells: Off you go, duck. If anything on your bike rattles, that's it asking to be a bell. Bring it round.
Ride gentle past Bench Four until Friday. It will be Bench *none* on Friday.
rumors: The Choir offered me a tithe in unbroken glass to hush my Sunday services. I took the glass and doubled the services. Church is church, duck.
They say the big cradle door past the glass hills is held by a lock as big as this yard. Rubbish, darling. A lock is a charge you haven't placed yet.
reactions: Ooh, that landing! All four corners complaining in harmony. You've a gift for percussion, duck.
You scuffed your paint. Good. A fast bike with unscuffed paint is a bicycle with ambitions.
lore: Anchor Seven's pods came down in one Sunday service — beautiful reading, standing ovation from the scaffold. The ancestors RSVP'd in thunder. We keep the blast log next to the prayer book; it's the same book, duck, different margins.
